To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synchronization of firm turnover and markups is a robust feature of the data and that this feature can be reproduced in a DSGEs with nominal frictions.
sticky prices are important for the synchronization of entry and markups and that this synchronization is important for the model to fit the data.
the comovement of entry and markups is driven by the synchronization of firm creation and firm exit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How does entry respond to shocks to aggregate demand? (2) How do entry decisions interact with markups?
a question that has received little attention so far: What are the implications of a model with sticky prices and endogenous markups for the dynamics of entry?
the role of nominal rigidities in the determination of markups and the synchronization of entry and markups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a model with sticky prices, monopolistic competition and entry, calibrated to U.S. data, is capable of generating realistic macroeconomic moments and a synchronization between firm entry and mark-ups.
a DSGE with nominal rigidities and firm entry is able to replicate the stylized facts of the macroeconomic data.
the model with entry and markups is consistent with the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synchronization of firm creation and price markups is an important mechanism for explaining the business cycle.
the model is able to match the comovement of entry and markups, but not the magnitude of the fluctuations in markups.
a model of firm entry and price stickiness can match the comovement of entry, markups, and inflation in the US data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model with nominal price rigidities is able to generate the synchronization of markups and entries observed in the data.
the synchronization between entry and markups is not only empirically relevant but can also be rationalized in a model that is consistent with other macroeconomic regularities.
a model with sticky prices, nominal rigidities, and endogenous firm entry can explain the observed synchronization between markups and entry.
